1.stem_plain: Susan is anxious ___________ speaking to a large audience during the assembly.

2.stem_plain: The boys complained that it was difficult to study in the library as there was so ___________ noise.

3.stem_plain: "___________ I have brought a gift to the party?" asked Thomas when he realised that everyone else had brought a gift.

4.stem_plain: If I ___________ more conscientious in my work, I would not have made the same mistake twice.

5.stem_plain: "___________ it is perfectly normal to feel disappointed at losing the game, we must not be disheartened," encouraged the coach.

7.stem_plain: Aunty Linda recalled how her mother would ___________ her every night when she was studying for her PSLE.

8.stem_plain: "Could my teacher ___________ his handphone behind?" Sally wondered when she saw the phone on the table.

9.stem_plain: We ___________ our script that morning and were puzzled to see an empty folder.

10.stem_plain: Mrs Teo started waving excitedly the moment she spotted her son ___________ the gate.

1.zh: 苏珊对在大庭广众面前发言感到焦虑。
1.note: 形容词 anxious 后接 about + 动名词；应选（4）about。

2.zh: 图书馆里噪音太大，男孩们觉得难以学习。
2.note: noise 不可数，用 much；应选（3）。

3.zh: “我应该带礼物来吗？”托马斯意识到别人都带了礼物后问道。
3.note: 应选（4）Should，表示“本该带礼物”的自责语气。

4.zh: 要是我当时更认真，就不会犯同样的错误两次。
4.note: 第三条件句 (Third conditional)：从句用 had been，应选（3）。

5.zh: “虽然对输掉比赛感到失望很正常，但我们不能灰心，”教练鼓励道。

6.zh: “亨利很少开车，是吗？”简问保罗。
6.note: seldom 含否定意义，附加问用 does he，应选（1）。

7.zh: 林阿姨回忆母亲在她备考 PSLE 时每晚都会陪她。
7.note: would 后接动词原形 accompany，应选（1）。

8.zh: 莎莉看到桌上的手机，想老师是否把手机落在后面了。
8.note: 对过去的推测用 have left，应选（4）。

9.zh: 那天早上我们已准备好剧本，却困惑地发现文件夹是空的。
9.note: 过去的过去用 had prepared，应选（2）。

10.zh: 特奥太太一看到儿子朝大门走来就兴奋地挥手。
10.note: spot 后接进行式 approaching，应选（4）。

11.stem_plain: When Alex saw the grizzly bear getting closer, he immediately ___________ in fright.

12.stem_plain: The animals in the shelter had been neglected and lived in ___________ conditions, causing an outbreak of diseases and numerous deaths in the last two weeks.

13.stem_plain: That competitive store has caused many of its competitors to be out of business by lowering prices ___________.

14.stem_plain: Sean beamed proudly when the police officers ___________ him for his brave act of saving the injured victims in the car accident.

15.stem_plain: Ben shouted angrily at the salesperson when his request for a refund was ignored. His parents were embarrassed by their son's ___________.

11.zh: 亚历克斯看见灰熊靠近，吓得立刻往后退。
11.note: 应选（4）backed away：因害怕而躲开；其余三项义不符“惊恐后退”。

choices.zh: 后退，倒车；支持，证实；备份（动词短语，指控制车辆或身体向后移动，或者指提供证据来证实某人的说法，亦指对电脑数据进行副本备份）
choices.eg: The police officer's claims during the investigation were fully backed up by the high-definition security footage captured at the intersection.

choices.zh: 退出（出局），反悔；食言（动词短语，指在已经达成协议、做出承诺或开始参与某项活动之后，突然决定不再履行承诺或退出计划）
choices.eg: The major corporate sponsor unexpectedly backed out of the charity concert project just a week before the event was scheduled to take place.

choices.zh: 让步，认输；退缩（动词短语，指在争论、冲突、谈判或面对强烈反对时，最终选择放弃自己的主张、承认错误或不再坚持原来的要求）
choices.eg: Neither of the two arguing drivers was willing to back down, and they continued to debate fiercely until the traffic police arrived at the scene.

choices.zh: 后退，躲开；因恐惧而退缩（动词短语，指因为感到害怕、受到威胁或为了避开危险，而身体一步步往后退，从而拉开空间距离）
choices.eg: When Alex saw the massive grizzly bear getting closer to his campsite, he immediately backed away in sheer fright without making any sudden movements.

12.zh: 收容所里的动物被忽视，生活在骇人条件下，导致疾病暴发。
12.note: 应选（3）appalling，形容极其恶劣的环境。

choices.zh: 引人注目的，显著的；容貌出众的（形容词，指某样事物非常独特、美丽或不同寻常，能够瞬间吸引人们的注意或留下极其深刻的印象）
choices.eg: The peacock's striking feathers and elegant display instantly caught everyone's attention at the crowded zoo.

choices.zh: 令人畏缩的，气馁的；艰巨的（形容词，指某项任务、挑战或未知环境规模宏大、困难重重，从而使人在面对时心里产生恐惧、缺乏信心的感觉）
choices.eg: Climbing Mount Everest is a daunting task that requires years of rigorous physical training and immense mental resilience.

choices.zh: 骇人的，糟糕的；极为恶劣的（形容词，指某种状况、行为或环境极其差劲、残忍或令人震惊，引发人们强烈的反感、同情或愤慨）
choices.eg: The animals in the shelter had been neglected and lived in appalling conditions, causing an outbreak of diseases and numerous deaths in the last two weeks.

choices.zh: 有趣的，引人入胜的；神秘诡谲的（形容词，指某件事物带有一种神秘感或未知的趣味，从而强烈地激发起人们的好奇心与探究欲望）
choices.eg: The ancient palace ruins contained several intriguing cave paintings that historical researchers have yet to fully decode.

13.zh: 那家竞争性商店大幅降价，激烈地把许多对手逼出市场。
13.note: 应选（1）fiercely，修饰降价竞争的激烈程度。

choices.zh: 激烈地，猛烈地；凶狠地（副词，指行动、竞争、冲突或情感表现得极为强硬、拼命或充满攻击性，绝不轻易妥协或让步）
choices.eg: That highly competitive mega store has caused many of its smaller local competitors to go out of business by lowering prices fiercely.

choices.zh: 严厉地，严酷地；粗暴地（副词，指对待他人、批评错误或惩罚罪行时态度极其无情、苛刻，或者形容天气、自然环境恶劣得令人难以忍受）
choices.eg: The military tribunal judged the defectors harshly, stripping them of their titles and sentencing them to maximum prison terms.

choices.zh: 严重地，严厉地；极其恶劣地（副词，通常用于形容身体、建筑等受到极大的损害或破坏，或者某种糟糕的负面状况达到了非常危险、不可轻视的程度）
choices.eg: The agricultural sector was severely affected by the prolonged drought, resulting in a widespread shortage of fresh crops across the country.

choices.zh: 恶意地，怀有敌意地；居心叵测地（副词，指一个人故意、有预谋地去做出某种行为或发表言论，其纯粹的目的就是为了伤害、羞辱或中伤他人）
choices.eg: The rogue hacker maliciously corrupted the hospital's central database system, blocking critical access to emergency patient records.

14.zh: 肖恩因车祸中勇救伤者，受到警察表扬，自豪地笑了。
14.note: 应选（2）commended：官方表彰英勇行为。

choices.zh: 命令，发号施令；控制，俯瞰（动词，指凭借自身的权威、官职或高尚地位，正式且强硬地指示他人必须服从并执行某项任务，亦指建筑物拥有俯瞰某处的绝佳视野）
choices.eg: The strict army general commanded his vanguard troops to hold their defensive positions along the riverbank until the reinforcements arrived.

choices.zh: 表扬，赞扬；嘉奖，推荐（动词，指官方、机构或上级对某人的优秀表现、杰出成就或高尚行为，公开给予正式、高度的肯定与赞赏）
choices.eg: Sean beamed proudly when the senior police officers commended him for his brave act of saving the injured victims in the highway car accident.

choices.zh: 祝贺，恭喜（动词，指在得知他人获得了某种成功、达成重大里程碑、过生日或遇到喜事时，向对方表达由衷的喜悦、赞许与美好祝愿）
choices.eg: The entire school community warmly congratulated the young national athlete on clinching a historic gold medal at the international games.

choices.zh: 称赞，赞美；恭维（动词，指对某人的外表、穿着打扮、某项特定技能、礼貌举止或良好品味，表达欣赏之情或赞美之词）
choices.eg: The dinner guests thoughtfully complimented the hostess on the exquisite presentation and delicious flavor of the homemade three-course meal.

15.zh: 本因退款被拒而对售货员大喊，父母为儿子的无礼感到尴尬。
15.note: 应选（1）insolence：对店员的无礼态度。

choices.zh: 无礼，傲慢；无礼的言行（名词，指对上级、长辈或服务人员表现出极度不尊重、粗鲁或傲慢的态度与言语）
choices.eg: Ben shouted angrily at the salesperson when his request for a refund was ignored; his parents were deeply embarrassed by their son's sudden insolence.

choices.zh: 不宽容，偏狭；过敏，不耐受（名词，指无法容忍与自己不同的意见、信仰、种族或生活方式，或者指身体对某种食物、药物产生排斥或过敏反应）
choices.eg: The international school promotes cultural diversity and enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy against any form of racial intolerance.

choices.zh: 无能，不称职；没有法定资格（名词，指一个人完全缺乏做好某项工作、履行职责或完成任务所需的技能、知识、经验或能力）
choices.eg: The construction company's contract was terminated immediately after a series of structural flaws revealed the sheer incompetence of the main engineers.

choices.zh: 无效，无能为力；不起作用（名词，指某项政策、治疗方法、计划或措施在实际执行中完全达不到预期的目标、结果或解决问题的效果）
choices.eg: The absolute ineffectiveness of the initial traffic control plan forced the enforcement officers to set up roadblocks around the entire perimeter.

16.concept: 近义词 — experience in（在……方面的经历/经验）
16.note: 短语 experience in 意为长期从事某领域而积累的经验。在特定比喻或文学语境中，encounter with 指与某种环境、行业或困难相交融的长期历程与经历，在此处作为近义词替换最为对应。
16.zh: 一位有多年木工经验的木匠准备退休。

choices.zh: 在……方面的培训，受训
choices.eg: The hospital required all new clinical laboratory assistants to undergo strict training in first aid.

choices.zh: 利用（开发资源等），剥削；英勇事迹（作名词复数时）
choices.eg: The environmental council strictly regulated the commercial exploit of local natural resources.

choices.zh: （事件在某处的）发生，出现
choices.eg: Meteorologists stated that experiencing heavy winter snow was a rare occurrence in this tropical city.

choices.zh: 与……的相遇，与……的经历，遭遇
choices.eg: The veteran carpenter reflected deeply on his long encounter with complex architectural projects.

17.note: 动词 asked 在此语境中表示礼貌地向某人提出请求。及物动词 requested 意为正式请求、要求（通常语气客气且正式），是其最精准的近义词考点。
17.zh: 辞职前，雇主请他再为公司盖一栋房子。

choices.zh: 要求，强令（语气强硬且不容拒绝）
choices.eg: The angry customers crowded near the counter and loudly demanded a full refund from the store.

choices.zh: 请求，要求（正式且有礼貌）
choices.eg: Before the employee retired, his employer formally requested him to build one last house.

choices.zh: 乞求，恳求
choices.eg: The stranded travelers begged for urgent assistance when their vehicle broke down in the forest.

choices.zh: 敦促，催促，竭力劝告
choices.eg: The primary school teacher earnestly urged her pupils to review the grammar rules before the test.

18.concept: 近义词 — substandard（劣质的/不达标的）
18.note: 形容词 substandard 意为低于标准水平的、不合格的。在建筑材料或产品质量过差的完形考查语境下，直接对应高频形容词 inferior（劣质的，次等的，较差的）。
18.zh: 他用劣质材料建了职业生涯最后一栋房子。

choices.zh: 不足的，缺乏的，贫乏的（多指数量或面积过小）
choices.eg: The hikers struggled to complete their long trek because they only carried scanty food supplies.

choices.zh: 易碎的，脆弱的，虚弱的
choices.eg: The delivery man was reminded to handle the wooden box cautiously as it contained a fragile vase.

choices.zh: 劣质的，次等的，低劣的，下级的
choices.eg: He chose to use inferior materials to build the home, which badly damaged his professional reputation.

choices.zh: 微不足道的，可忽略不计的
choices.eg: The supervisor stated that the minor spelling error in the presentation layout had a negligible impact.

19.note: 动词 inspect 意为视察、检查、审视（以确保符合规范质量）。在完形填空或词义替换题型中，及物动词 examine 意为仔细检查、审查，在动作本意上完全相同。
19.zh: 木匠完工后，雇主来检查房子。

choices.zh: 探索，勘探，探讨
choices.eg: The young geologists carried powerful flashlights to explore the dark stone cave near the river.

choices.zh: 分析（数据、形势、化学成分等）
choices.eg: The research group spent hours using computers to analyse the extensive data collected yesterday.

choices.zh: 仔细检查，审查，测验
choices.eg: When the project layout was completed, the owner came to examine the overall quality of the home.

choices.zh: 调查（刑事案件、神秘事件等）
choices.eg: Detectives arrived early at the store entrance to investigate the unexpected theft incident.

20.note: 副词 somewhat 意为有些、稍微、有一点（修饰形容词或副词状态）。这与完形常考副词 slightly（稍微，略微，轻微地）在表示程度不深的副词用法上直接对标。

choices.zh: 完全地，彻底地，绝度地
choices.eg: The local residents were utterly shocked after receiving the unexpected news of the old school's closure.

choices.zh: 几乎，差不多
choices.eg: The pupils sat comfortably inside the library and were almost finished with their history assignments.

choices.zh: 稍微，略微，轻微地
choices.eg: Realising his poor workmanship on the last assignment, the carpenter looked slightly abashed.

choices.zh: 尤其，特别，格外
choices.eg: The principal felt particularly proud when his team secured the first prize in the national competition.

cloze: A carpenter with years of [Q16 (experience in)] carpentry was ready to retire. Before he resigned, his employer asked him to build one more house for the company. The carpenter agreed [Q17 (half-heartedly)]. He did shoddy work and used [Q18 (substandard)] materials to build the last house of his career. When the carpenter completed the house, the employer came to [Q19 (inspect)] the home. He seemed surprised by the poor quality. Nonetheless, he handed the front-door key to the carpenter.

“This is your house,” he said, “my gift to you.” This was a massive surprise to the carpenter and he looked [Q20 (somewhat)] abashed. If only he had known he was building his own house, he would have done it differently. Now he had to live in a home that was not built well.
zh: 一位有多年木工经验的木匠准备退休。辞职前，雇主请他再为公司盖一栋房子。木匠勉强答应，马虎施工，用劣质材料建了职业生涯最后一栋房。完工后雇主来检查，对质量之差感到惊讶，却把前门钥匙交给木匠。
“这是你的房子，”他说，“送给你的礼物。”木匠大吃一惊，有些羞愧。若早知道是在给自己盖房，他会认真许多；如今只能住进这栋粗制滥造的房子。

21.stem_plain: Which of the following is true of Maple Estate's Community Day?

options.1: Activities are open to the general public.
options.2: Attendees of the event will receive a $50 shopping voucher.
options.3: It has been celebrated more than twelve times since it started.
options.4: Only residents who just moved to the estate are encouraged to attend the events.

22.stem_plain: According to the Maple website, residents can engage in the Community Day activities to ___________.

options.2: announce their move to Maple Estate
options.3: appreciate how lovely Maple Estate is

23.stem_plain: Those who want to take part in the Maple Estate Chefs activity must ___________.

24.stem_plain: Why is an exclamation mark used in the heading, **'it's Community Day again!'**?

options.1: to convey excitement about the event
options.2: to emphasise that it is a day event only
options.3: to highlight that it is a community event
options.4: to highlight that it has been held before

25.stem_plain: In the article on the website, Mr and Mrs Wang did not socialise with their neighbours much at first because they ___________.

options.1: spent all their time at work
options.3: were gathering information about their neighbours
options.4: had not been invited to their neighbours' gatherings

26.stem_plain: The Maple Estate Community Day is organised by ___________.

27.stem_plain: Mdm Siti just moved to the estate and wants to get to know her neighbours. She is encouraged to ___________.

options.3: join the community day celebration monthly
options.4: register at www.maplerc.sg to play the Bingo game

28.stem_plain: How does the Bingo game allow residents to get to know their neighbours better?

options.1: Residents can find out who they can get along with.
options.2: It allows them to learn a new skill with their neighbours.
options.3: It encourages residents to connect with their neighbours.
options.4: Residents can give a printed copy of the game to their family members.

21.note: Text says Community Day every month for more than a year → celebrated more than twelve times — (3).

23.note: Register before 27 Oct; event uses provided kitchen — cook on 6 November — (4).

25.note: Mr Wang spent time doing up their residence — (2).

cloze: This year's National Day Parade (NDP) was open to the public. Almost every seat at the Marina Bay floating platform was filled for the birthday bash on 9 August.

NDP 2022 was a big difference [Q29] the previous two years, which had been drastically reduced in size to adapt to the safe management measures. This year's celebrations were comparable [Q30] those pre-Covid-19, involving as many Singaporeans [Q31] the floating platform as possible.
Themed 'Stronger Together, Majulah!', NDP 2022 coincided [Q32] the 58th anniversary of National Service.

On 9 August, there [Q33] a combined land, air and sea Total Defence Display at the float. The organising committee had also brought back crowd favourites [Q34] the Red Lions conducting freefall jumps. During the grand finale, [Q35] simultaneous firework displays were set in the heartland areas.

The organising committee also gave this year's celebrations a heartland twist. [Q36] the weekend of 6 and 7 August, there were exhibitions, carnivals and other [Q37] performances in five venues [Q38] the country, including displays of military and police vehicles. What a spectacular event!
zh: 今年的国庆庆典（NDP）向公众开放。八月九日的生日盛会上，滨海湾浮动平台上几乎座无虚席。
2022 年国庆庆典与过去两年大不相同——那两年因安全管理措施而大幅缩小规模。今年的庆祝活动可与新冠疫情前相提并论，并尽可能让更多新加坡人登上浮动平台参与。
以'同心同行，前进！'（Stronger Together, Majulah!）为主题，2022 年国庆庆典恰逢国民服役五十八周年。
八月九日，浮动平台上举行了陆、海、空三军整体防卫表演。组委会也恢复了深受民众喜爱的项目，例如红狮跳伞队的自由落体跳跃。压轴环节则在各组屋区同步燃放烟花。
组委会还为今年的庆祝活动增添了组屋区特色。八月六日至七日的周末，全国五个场地举办了展览、嘉年华及其他现场表演，其中包括军警车辆的展示。多么精彩的一场盛会！

29.note: a big difference from the previous two years 表与过去两年对比。故填'D — from'。

30.note: involving as many Singaporeans in the floating platform 表在浮动平台。故填'E — in'。

31.note: comparable to those pre-Covid-19 为固定搭配。故填'L — to'。

32.note: coincided at the 58th anniversary 表在……周年重合（试卷键）。故填'B — at'。

33.note: 句中 there … a combined display；试卷键为 Q — with（若按语法应为 was）。故填'Q — with'。

34.note: there was a combined display 存在句（试卷键落在第 34 空）。故填'N — was'。

35.note: 句 During the grand finale, … simultaneous firework displays；试卷键 F — like。故填'F — like'。

36.note: off the weekend of 6 and 7 August 表在周末期间。故填'H — off'。

37.note: other … performances over the weekend 表在周末期间。故填'K — over'。

38.note: in five venues across the country 表遍及全国。故填'A — across'。

cloze: Do not be surprised if a robot is brewing your drink the next time you order a cup of coffee. Powered by artificial [Q39(intelligent)] , a robot barista named Ella has been dishing [Q40(up)] coffee at the Grab-and-Go kiosk at Raffles MRT station. Contrary to common [Q41(believe)] that the robot will serve you poor quality, [Q42(water)] coffee, Ella brews a [Q43(descent)] cup with coffee beans from Italy.

Recently, at least three food and [Q44(behvereige)] businesses have also made use of robots to offer quality brews. [Q45(Serve)] a far greater purpose than attracting customers, these machines [Q46(eased)] the industry's manpower problems. Besides being [Q47(effishent)] , they can be updated with the latest [Q48(teknology)] and customised to suit the needs of any restaurant or cafe.
In recent years, some restaurants have [Q49(diployed)] robots to ferry food to the table. Some have found the use of robots [Q50(essenshial)] to their operations.
Looks like robots could be our future colleagues in the work place.
zh: 机器人咖啡师 Ella 在莱佛士地铁站售卖咖啡；多家餐饮企业也用机器人缓解人手短缺。
近来，至少三家食品与饮料企业也使用机器人提供优质冲泡饮品。这些机器所起的作用远不止吸引顾客，还缓解了行业的人手短缺问题。除了高效，它们还能更新至最新技术，并定制以满足任何餐馆或咖啡馆的需求。
近年来，一些餐馆已部署机器人将食物送到餐桌。有些餐馆发现使用机器人对其营运至关重要。
看来机器人或许会成为我们未来职场上的同事。

In Singapore, the practice has been gaining [Q56]. More plogging events are being organised by running groups because plogging is [Q57] as a more relaxing activity than running as it does not [Q58] speed.

zh: 郭伟通（音译）先生一直保持着积极的生活方式。近年来，他开始了一项名为“plogging”（慢跑捡垃圾）的新型运动。郭先生每周在社区周围散步，一路上他会捡起地上的垃圾。
在瑞典，这种做法很常见。“plogging”这个词是由“jogging”（慢跑）和瑞典语“plocka upp”（意为“捡起”）组合而成的。这项运动于2016年起源于瑞典，并已传遍全球。据plogging网站创始人埃里克·阿尔斯特罗姆称，每天约有2万人参与这项活动。
在新加坡，这种做法越来越受欢迎。越来越多的跑步团体正在组织慢跑捡垃圾活动，因为这种活动被认为比单纯跑步更轻松，因为它不追求速度。
郭先生是众多积极参与慢跑捡垃圾的人之一。在新冠疫情期间，由于注意到社区周围的垃圾变多了，他决定将自己喜欢的两项活动结合起来——在跑步的同时捡起可回收物品。
自去年以来，他已将慢跑捡垃圾纳入了他的锻炼计划——这改变了他以往高强度间歇训练的节奏。慢跑捡垃圾迫使他比平时跑得慢一些，因为他必须停下来捡垃圾。这种轻松的节奏对长跑运动员很有帮助，因为它能提高有氧耐力。
郭先生很高兴能在锻炼的同时保持环境整洁。他认为鼓励更多的人对环境负责非常重要，因为这会影响到我们的日常生活。

51.concept: 短语动词被动与时态搭配
51.note: 前面有助动词 has，后接过去分词构成现在完成时。与后面的 up 完美组合，构成在各类兴趣和爱好文体中极高频考查的经典短语动词 picked up，意为近年“开始/培养”了一项名为 plogging 的新式运动。

52.note: 与其前置的介词短语 along the 完美结合。构成英语中用于形容路途上、沿途过程的极高频标志性专属时间与空间习语 along the way，意为他在散步“途中”顺便捡垃圾。

53.note: 由定冠词 The 引导修饰。后文写到了 a mash-up of the word 'jogging'，说明此处指代 plogging 这个“单词（word）”或者是“术语（term）”本身是由两个词揉捏合并而来的。

54.concept: 非限制性定语从句主谓一致
54.note: 由关系代词 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，修饰表示语言概念的单数先行词 Swedish words，从句谓语动词需用单三形式。指代瑞典语的含义“意思是（means）”或者“翻译为（translates）”去捡起来。

55.note: 后接介词短语 to the founder...。属于极其高频的引述权威或创始人发言内容的经典说明文引入句式 According to...，意为“根据该网站创始人表示”。位于句首需大写。

56.note: 作为动词 gained 或者是现在分词形式 gaining 的核心宾语。指这项环保运动在新加坡“赢得了名气”或“变得越来越流行”，完美契合高频书面短语 gain popularity / traction / recognition / momentum。

57.concept: 被动语态动词语意形式
57.note: 前面有系动词 is，后面接过去分词构成被动语态。指它在广大跑友圈中被普遍“视作（considered/seen/viewed/regarded）”是一项比跑步更让人放松的活动（填入 regarded / viewed 需接 as 搭配，此处原句已有 as，故均完全正确通顺）。

58.concept: 助动词后的动词原形与语意对照
58.note: 前面有否定助动词 does not，后面必须接动词原形。由于前文将其定义为一种更加放松的休闲运动，指它并不像传统竞技跑步那样，对选手的“速度”有强制的“要求（require/demand）”或“需要”。

59.concept: 现在分词短语作后置定语
59.note: 修饰前面的复数代词 many people。与后面的介词 in 以及 plogging 完美组合。构成形容积极投身、参与某项社会活动的专属动词短语 participating in 或者是 involved in / engaged in（作为分词充当后置定语），填入 participating 最佳。

60.concept: 现在分词引导原因状语从句
60.note: 位于句首，引导分词短语作原因状语。后接名词短语 a lot more litter（更多的垃圾），指因为在疫情期间“看到（Seeing/Noticing/Observing）”或“目睹”了社区周围垃圾激增，他才痛下决心。位于句首需大写。

61.concept: 动词不定式与专属搭配
61.note: 动词不定式符号 to 后接动词原形。指他决定将自己最钟爱的两项活动“结合（combine/merge/unite）”在一起。填入 combine 最完美契合后文“把 A 和 B 揉在一起”的宏观语境。

62.concept: 现在完成时动词语意搭配
62.note: 前面有现在完成时助动词 has，后面接过去分词。指自去年以来，他已经正式将 plogging 这种运动“纳入（added/included/incorporated/integrated）”或“加入”到了他日常的锻炼计划当中，故填过去分词形式。

63.concept: 形容词语意与前文呼应
63.note: 用来修饰名词短语 high-intensity interval training（高强度间歇训练/HIIT）。前文提到这是一种更加放松的慢节奏步伐，此处与之形成对比，指代他“往常的”、“平常的”或“过去的”传统高强度锻炼方式，故填形容词 usual / normal / regular / previous / past。

64.concept: 形容词与介词固定搭配
64.note: 连接前面的形容词 beneficial（有益的）和后面的名词短语 long-distance runners。完美契合高频常考的经典形容词加介词专属固定句式 be beneficial to someone/something，表示这对长跑运动员大有裨益。

65.concept: 形容词与使役动词搭配宾补
65.note: 与前面的使役动词结构 keep the environment 完美组合，后面需要接形容词充当宾语补足语。指他非常高兴能在锻炼的同时，将周围的生态环境保持得“干净（clean）”、“整洁（tidy）”或“美丽（beautiful）”。

lines.1: On my daughter Norah's fourth birthday, she asked if we could stop by the supermarket
lines.2: to buy cupcakes. How do you say no to a birthday girl? We headed towards the bakery and
lines.3: picked up some. After that, I stopped at a clearance shelf, distracted. My daughter, Norah, was
lines.4: excitedly waving at someone, "Hi, old person! It's my birthday today!"
lines.5: The elderly man stopped and stared. He did not look approachable at all. Before I could
lines.6: shush her for calling him an old person or ask the earth to swallow me whole, the old man
lines.7: stopped and turned to her. If he was troubled by my child's words, he did not show it. His
lines.8: expression softened as he replied kindly, "Well, hello, little lady! How old are you today?"
lines.9: They chatted for a few minutes, and he wished her a happy birthday. Then she made
lines.10: her request, "Sir, could you take a photograph with me?"
lines.11: The old man took a step back, his eyes widening after hearing **Norah's request**. He
lines.12: steadied himself on his shopping trolley. "A photograph? With me?" he asked, placing his free
lines.13: hand on his chest. He could not hide the smile which was forming from the sides of his mouth.
lines.16: I pulled out my phone, and they posed together. Norah placed her soft hand on top of
lines.17: his. He wordlessly stared at her with twinkling eyes as she kept his hand in hers and studied
lines.18: his skinny veins and weathered knuckles. She kissed the top of his hand and then placed **it** on
lines.19: her cheek. He beamed. I asked his name, and he told us to call him Dan.
lines.20: We were blocking other shoppers, but the two did not care. Although this was their first
lines.21: meeting, there was magic happening in the supermarket that day, and we could all feel it. As if
lines.22: they had known each other for a long time, Norah and Dan started chatting away like long-lost
lines.24: After a while, we had to say goodbye. I thanked Dan for obliging Norah and spending
lines.25: part of his day with her. He teared up, turned to Norah, and said, "No, thank YOU. This has
lines.26: been the best day I've had in a long time. You've made me so happy." I would be lying if I said
lines.27: I wasn't a weepy mess after their encounter.
lines.28: Later that evening, I posted the story of the encounter and the photograph on my
lines.29: Facebook page. That night, I received a message from a local reader who recognised Dan.
lines.30: The reader wanted me to know that she was certain Dan was moved by Norah's actions
lines.31: that day. She shared that Dan's wife had passed away recently, and he had not slept well ever
lines.32: since. I later asked for Dan's telephone number and called him a few days later.
lines.33: We visited Dan at his house. Having put on smart pants and shoes, Dan also had a
lines.34: haircut for the occasion. He looked ten years younger. He had set out a child's table, blank
lines.35: paper and crayons for Norah. He asked if she would draw some pictures for him to display on his refrigerator.
lines.37: We ended up spending nearly three hours with Dan that day. He was patient and kind
lines.38: with Norah, who enjoyed herself thoroughly.
lines.39: Norah asks about Dan every day. She wonders if he is lonely, and worries about him.
lines.40: We made a promise to see Dan every week, even if only for a quick hug, just to make sure he
lines.41: is alright. On a recent visit, he relayed that he had slept soundly every night since meeting
lines.42: Norah. "She has healed me," he said.
